findings.message: The three font preloads in src/_partials/_head.erb make first paint 2.5 to 3.5 times slower on every route, profile and protocol measured. They remove the cold-font layout shift only in simulated Lighthouse. Mechanism: the 123 KiB of preloaded woff2 shares bandwidth with the 38 KiB render-blocking stylesheet, so the CSS finishes about 3 times later, and the fonts arrive no sooner. HTTP/2 (Caddy, TLS, CDP-throttled, 5 runs, medians): / at 1.6 Mbps FCP 632 ms vs 252 ms without the preload, at 400 kbit/s 1224 vs 388 ms. /portfolio/ 652 vs 240 and 1272 vs 380 ms. CLS is the same with or without the preload: / 0.140, /portfolio/ 0.184. HTTP/1.1 (same snapshot): / 1160 vs 372 ms at 1.6 Mbps, where CLS does go from 0.140 to 0 because paint waits for the fonts, and 3336 vs 968 ms at 400 kbit/s. Devtools Lighthouse: / 2032 vs 1444 ms. The frame strip shows the shift's cause: in the fallback face the header nav wraps 'SUOMEKSI' onto a second line, and PT Sans fits it on one. Fix: remove the three preloads. Then give the fallback stacks metric-matched @font-face rules (local Arial/Georgia with size-adjust, ascent-override and descent-override tuned to PT Sans and PT Serif), so the swap moves nothing and first paint stays early. If a preload stays, keep at most the one face the first viewport needs, and show by an observed measurement that FCP doesn't regress. Limits: Caddy's Go HTTP/2 server schedules round-robin, and devtools throttling happens on the client. A CDN that sends the Highest-priority stylesheet first could shrink the FCP cost, but nothing suggests it would fix the shift.

Carried from review 4bd5d688, updated. Six D20 LCP rows remain after this change, down from 14 timing rows. They are the existing cost of the web fonts each page renders: LCP equals the first text paint, and render delay grows with the number of faces. Simulated Lighthouse after the preload: /portfolio/, /services/ and /about/ at about 2252 ms against the 2000 ms static budget. They still need an owner (opportunity O-c2). The fix path is the one F8 gives, not more preloads: metric-matched fallbacks, and dropping PT Sans 400 italic where headings only fake a bold italic. Re-run perf and delete the rows that pass.

Carried from review 5c2e92ac, unchanged and pre-existing. Footer text fails WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.3 on every page, and no retrofit row records it. On linear-gradient(#e8e8e8, #cccccc), the 12.8 px #888888 text reaches 2.21 to 2.89:1 and the #666666 links reach 3.58 to 4.69:1, where 4.5:1 is required. axe can't decide over the gradient, so the gate only warns. The footer markup and CSS are untouched by this diff, and the font is the same PT Sans. It doesn't block adoption, but it blocks any change to the footer. Fix: #555555 or darker for footer text (4.64:1 on #cccccc), or a flat background. Until then, record it explicitly.
